source.source_title: I don't love the current version of the Web Browser control surface…

procedural: Please run /login
WebBrowser.tsx (738 lines, all CSS inline) renders a Chrome-lookalike chrome
next to a 380px BrowserControlPanel that fronts three unrelated transports: TNF Browser (:7331), the legacy Chrome-extension relay (:3000), and Federation channels.
WebBrowser.tsx:376 renders previewShot
useTnfBrowser.ts:194 runs an 8-second timer that refreshes status only.
The top strip (WebBrowser.tsx:28) is local React state seeded with a fake about:blank tab.
The real Chrome tabs live in the panel's read-only "Tabs (N)" list (BrowserControlPanel.tsx:421)
tabs.create, tabs.close, tabs.activate all exist in the protocol and none are wired.
This is the package's whole differentiator: a 15-step safe-interaction pipeline, avoid rules, honeypot detection, bezier cursor paths (PROTOCOL.md:202-217).
tnf_browser_bridge.rs:155-164 parses event frames, handles extensionConnected/extensionDisconnected, then continues
WebBrowser.tsx:210,218 call browser.goBack()/goForward() unconditionally
The button appears in two places (WebBrowser.tsx:321, BrowserControlPanel.tsx:296), never changes state, and only works in the dev Vite bridge.
applyUrlToTab (WebBrowser.tsx:69-81) shallow-copies the array then mutates the element in place
:297 puts http://127.0.0.1:3000/health in the new-tab shortcut grid next to "Example" and "TNF Docs".
It opens raw JSON.
- Panel tabs are <button>s with no role/aria-selected (BrowserControlPanel.tsx:102-124), and an arbitrary 1.2fr 0.8fr 1fr grid.
vite.config.ts:340 sets host: '0.0.0.0', and /__tnf-browser/command has no authentication
In practice you're safe: the dev script passes --host 127.0.0.1 and I confirmed the live process is loopback-bound (curl from 192.168.1.103 refused).
The surface was designed as "a browser" and then had a protocol bolted behind it.
A text field + Enter next to the click selector is ~15 lines and closes the biggest capability hole.
strategic: Make tnf.tabs the only tab model; wire click
A text field + Enter next to the click selector is ~15 lines and closes the biggest capability hole.
governance: Now let me audit what the actual TNF Browser runtime protocol supports vs.
I audited the running surface, the React page, both bridges (Vite dev + Rust), and the tnf-browser protocol it's supposed to drive.
Closing a strip tab calls no protocol action; opening a real Chrome tab never appears in the strip.
tabs.create, tabs.close, tabs.activate all exist in the protocol and none are wired.
This is the package's whole differentiator: a 15-step safe-interaction pipeline, avoid rules, honeypot detection, bezier cursor paths (PROTOCOL.md:202-217).
The protocol hands you live navigation events for free; the UI polls status every 8s instead and only learns the URL changed if the user clicks something.
Worse: the TNF protocol has no history action at all (no goBack in service-worker.js).
The protocol ships dom.boundingBox and dom.setDebug plus a cursor overlay precisely so you could highlight-before-acting.
it will proxy any protocol action into your logged-in Chrome.
The surface was designed as "a browser" and then had a protocol bolted behind it.
